speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the skin lesions, including when they first appeared and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the lesions umbilicated with a central dimple, and do they have a pearly or waxy appearance? I also need to check if there are any lesions on her face, scalp, or extremities.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the characteristic pearly, umbilicated papules and the daycare exposure, this presentation is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
